_comment: Brain profiles. Copy to config/brains.json and edit. Select with WIKI_BRAIN=<name>|auto and WIKI_BRAIN_DATA=public|personal|company|private (default company). 'data' = the data classes this brain may receive: company = company documents, personal = your own notes, private = notes marked private (diary...), public = public material. A brain not listed for a class is NEVER used for it, not even as a fallback. 'cost': lower is tried first in auto mode (0 = free/local). Keys: only files (api_key_file; a key value written in this JSON is rejected). Put the key file OUTSIDE this repo folder (e.g. under your user profile, readable only by you); a relative path would be relative to this file. Each brain sees ONLY its own settings (nothing is inherited). Check with: python -m llmwiki.brains list

gemini._comment: Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (UNVERIFIED here: check the address and model id in Google's docs). Sends text to Google: allow only what your policy allows. On-site company documents: ask security first (leave 'company' out until approved).

gemini-corp._comment: ON-SITE ONLY, and only after security approves sending company documents to Gemini: the COMPANY-issued Gemini access (its own address and its own key file, NOT your personal key). 'company' is listed here on purpose; the personal 'gemini' profile above never receives company documents. Use with WIKI_BRAIN=gemini-corp (or auto) and WIKI_BRAIN_DATA=company. Consider WIKI_PII_POLICY_FILE masking for the spaces you send (regex based, not complete).
